conversation.content:
Hello! I’m glad we have a few minutes to sit together. I’m <med>Dr. Maya Bennett</med>, a perinatal mental-health clinician here to support new moms as they adjust to life after birth.  

Today we’ll use a short questionnaire called the <sym>Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale</sym> (often called the EPDS). It’s a well-trusted tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past week. This isn’t a test—there are no right or wrong answers—and your responses stay confidential within the care team. We simply want to make sure we’re giving you the best support possible.

I’ll ask 10 questions, and the best answer is whatever feels most true for you. We can pause anytime, and if anything feels overwhelming, we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to start?

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things—would you say you’ve enjoyed a good laugh as much as usual, not quite as much, or hardly at all?
I guess I can still laugh sometimes, but… it doesn’t feel quite the same. Like, I’ll chuckle if my partner jokes around, but it fades fast. I’d say I’m laughing “not quite as much” as I used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah… like I said, I can laugh a little, but it feels kind of flat. I’ll smile or chuckle, but it doesn’t last or feel as good as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to some things—like when my mom visits or when I get to take the baby for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it was before I had him. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of really counting down the hours.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Like, when he wouldn’t settle at 3 a.m. I kept thinking maybe I’m not feeding him right or holding him the “best” way. I know it’s probably not really my fault, but the thought still pops in and makes me feel kind of lousy.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes, yeah. Like I’ll suddenly wonder if the baby’s breathing when he’s napping, even though I just checked. It hits out of nowhere and I feel my heart race a bit, but I can usually calm myself down pretty quickly. It’s not constant—just a few times this week.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky—more like a quick flash of “what if something’s wrong?” when he’s quiet in the crib. It’s gone almost as soon as I peek at him, so I wouldn’t call it scared or panicky, just a little anxious for a minute.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. Like yesterday—he wouldn’t nap unless I held him, the laundry piled up, and I felt behind on everything. For a minute I thought, “I can’t do all this,” but I took a breath, put him in the wrap, and got through it. So it’s happened, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt that way most of the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, I don’t feel that kind of unhappy. I do have a little trouble falling asleep sometimes—my mind races through the feeding schedule or whether I packed the diaper bag right—but once I’m out, I’m out. It’s not that I’m too sad or upset to sleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad once in a while—like, yesterday evening I just suddenly teared up while folding onesies. It passed after a few minutes, so I’m not walking around miserable all day, just… sad moments that come and go.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… that happened twice this week. Once when he wouldn’t latch and I felt stuck on the couch for an hour, and once when my partner found me in the nursery at 2 a.m. Both times the tears just came, but I was able to settle pretty soon after.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired or overwhelmed, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary – [Date]

**Symptoms & Findings**  
- **Mood**: episodic tearfulness, transient sad mood, diminished pleasure/enjoyment (“flat” laughter, muted anticipation)  
- **Affect**: reactive, not persistently low  
- **Guilt/Self-blame**: present (infant-care perceptions)  
- **Anxiety**: situational, infant-focused worries with rapid self-resolution; no panic equivalents  
- **Coping**: occasional “can’t do all this” thoughts; able to re-ground and complete tasks  
- **Sleep**: onset delay related to racing thoughts, not mood-anchored insomnia  
- **Crying spells**: twice this week, brief, linked to feeding/overnight stress  
- **Appetite/Concentration**: not assessed  
- **Self-harm ideation**: denied (endorsed item 10 negative)  

**Pattern**  
Intermittent mild depressive and anxiety symptoms, situationally triggered, with intact resilience and no functional impairment beyond transient overwhelm.  

**Screening Significance**  
Meets some criteria for **minor / subsyndromal postpartum depression & anxiety**; does not meet threshold for major depressive episode or generalized anxiety disorder at present.  

**Risk Factors**  
- Persistent stress if symptoms intensify or prolong  
- Possible escalation to major depression if support diminishes or sleep deprivation worsens  
- **Protective**: denies self-harm, reports partner/maternal support, uses active coping strategies  

**Next Steps (Screening Level)**  
Continue monitoring with Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) in 1–2 weeks; psychoeducation on postpartum mood changes, sleep hygiene, and prompt re-contact if mood worsens, enjoyment further declines, or any self-harm ideation develops.
